Estimate grid-resolution data from grouped observations

Source: R/harmonise-ungroup.R
mt_ungroup.Rd

Fills the modelling grid (single years of age by default) from deaths and exposures observed in coarser age groups, using the penalized composite link model (PCLM; Eilers 2007, Rizzi et al. 2015).

Usage

mt_ungroup(
  data,
  age = NULL,
  dims = 1,
  method = c("pclm", "monotone", "hyman_kannisto", "natural_gompertz", "gam"),
  exposure_method = c("pclm", "monotone"),
  lambda = NULL,
  criterion = c("bic", "aic"),
  kr = 2,
  deg = 3,
  pord = 2,
  lambda_range = c(0.01, 1e+08),
  preserve_totals = TRUE,
  tail = c("kannisto", "gompertz"),
  tail_width = 2
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

age

Target age axis (mt_axis). By default the grid when it was set (with mt_set_grid() or step_grid()) and is finer than the data, otherwise single years of age from the lowest age to the start of the open interval.

dims

1 or 2.

method

Method for deaths: "pclm" (default); "monotone" (cumulative deaths interpolated by a monotone Hyman spline, counts only, 1D, ignores exposures); or rate-based spline methods, which need exposures on the grid: "hyman_kannisto" (monotone spline of log group rates with a Kannisto tail for the open interval), "natural_gompertz" (natural spline with a log-linear tail) and "gam" (2D tensor-product GAM of log group rates over age and year with a Kannisto tail, package mgcv). All three preserve the exposure-weighted group rates exactly. Median absolute log errors against single-year rates (England & Wales men 1980-2011, 5-year groups to 90-100; and the simulated mt_example() with deaths to 90+): PCLM 0.015/0.024 and 0.012/0.006 (ages 30-89/90+), "hyman_kannisto" 0.015/0.029 and 0.013/0.028, "natural_gompertz" 0.015/0.027 and 0.013/0.030, "gam" 0.015/0.031 and 0.012/0.031. PCLM is the most accurate in the open interval; the spline methods are 5 to 10 times faster.

exposure_method

"pclm" or "monotone".

lambda

Fixed smoothing parameter(s); NULL selects them by criterion.

criterion

"bic" or "aic".

kr

Knot spacing in years (age and period).

deg, pord

Degree of the B-splines and order of the difference penalty.

lambda_range

Search range for the smoothing parameters.

preserve_totals

Rescale estimates to observed group totals.

tail, tail_width

For method = "gam": the parametric curve that takes over from the GAM above the start of the last age group ("kannisto", logistic, or "gompertz", log-linear), fitted to the GAM rates from age 70, and the width (years) of the logistic blend between the two.

Value

An mt_data object with deaths (and exposures) on the grid. Diagnostics per fit are attached as attribute "ungroup": smoothing parameters, effective dimension, the largest relative difference between fitted and observed group totals before rescaling, and a flag when a smoothing parameter is at the boundary of the search range.

Details

  • Exposures observed coarser than the grid are ungrouped first, as counts (exposure_method = "pclm") or by a monotone spline of the cumulative counts ("monotone", Hyman filter), which preserves group totals exactly.

  • Deaths are ungrouped as rates when exposures are available on the grid: the exposures enter as offset, so cohort-size waves stay in the exposures and the estimated rate schedule is smooth. Without exposures, deaths are ungrouped as counts per year of age (1D only; 2D smoothing of death counts cannot represent cohort waves and is refused).

  • The open age interval is expanded into single years up to omega; for rates the exposure of the open interval is spread with stationary-population weights implied by the fitted rates.

  • dims = 1 fits each stratum and period separately; dims = 2 fits a smooth age-period surface per stratum (two smoothing parameters).

With preserve_totals = TRUE, the estimated deaths within each observed group are rescaled to the observed total, so aggregation reproduces the data exactly. Cells already observed at grid resolution are kept.

In backtests use step_ungroup() so that ungrouping, in particular in 2D, sees only the training window.

References

Eilers PHC (2007). Ill-posed problems with counts, the composite link model and penalized likelihood. Statistical Modelling 7(3): 239-254.

Rizzi S, Gampe J, Eilers PHC (2015). Efficient estimation of smooth distributions from coarsely grouped data. American Journal of Epidemiology 182(2): 138-147. doi:10.1093/aje/kwv020

Examples

x <- mt_example(years = 2010:2014)
u <- mt_ungroup(x)
u
#> <mt_data> 2 strata by sex, omega = 110
#>   deaths     single years 30-99, 100+; periods 2010-2014 (width 1); 710 cells
#>   exposure   single years 30-99, 100+; periods 2010-2014 (width 1); 710 cells
#>   grid       <mt_axis: age, 71 intervals> 30 31 32 33 ... 98 99 100+
#>              <mt_axis: period, 5 intervals> 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014
head(attr(u, "ungroup"))
#>    measure stratum period       method lambda_age lambda_period       ed
#>     <char>   <int> <char>       <char>      <num>         <num>    <num>
#> 1:  deaths       1   2010 pclm_rate_1d  19515.370            NA 6.448288
#> 2:  deaths       1   2011 pclm_rate_1d  27584.317            NA 6.086148
#> 3:  deaths       1   2012 pclm_rate_1d   7094.886            NA 7.545750
#> 4:  deaths       1   2013 pclm_rate_1d   2340.520            NA 8.833281
#> 5:  deaths       1   2014 pclm_rate_1d   1880.462            NA 9.096312
#> 6:  deaths       2   2010 pclm_rate_1d  18039.474            NA 6.841390
#>    max_rel_diff at_bound
#>           <num>   <lgcl>

#> 2:   0.06301502    FALSE
